subject: Standby GPU commitment for late-stage POC — provisional hold request
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@aequitas.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@aequitas.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Oct 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Standby request + rough sizing for POC (timeline: Nov)

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our engineering team is confident we can run the POC in November, but before we lock dates we need a short standby/soft-hold on capacity while procurement finishes PO approvals. We expect peak model usage for the POC will be the 70B variant with mixed-precision (4-bit quantized) and an expected concurrency of ~35 sessions, average prompt+generation ~900 tokens, target p99 latency <700ms. Rough ask below:

- Duration: 4 weeks (target window: 2029-11-04 to 2029-12-02)
- Equivalent GPUs (estimated): 18x A100-80GB (or equivalent capacity) — this includes a ~10% buffer.
- Need: provisional hold until 2029-10-28 to finalize PO.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can place a short standby hold for that window and what the cancellation/penalty terms would be? Attaching the draft MA and our initial sizing sheet.

Appreciate a quick read — procurement is on a tight cadence.

Best,
Samir Khan
Head of Infrastructure, Aequitas Labs
attachments: AEQ_Draft_MA.pdf (pdf), initial-sizing-sheet.csv (csv)
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@aequitas.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@aequitas.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Oct 2029 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Standby request + rough sizing for POC (timeline: Nov)

Samir —

Thanks for the clear numbers and the attachments. We can provision a provisional standby allocation while procurement finishes the PO, but we need to lock a few internal checks first:

- Confirm exact model variant and quantization profile (you mentioned 70B, 4-bit). If you can confirm FP16 vs 4-bit for the final run, that changes node counts.
- Confirm expected sustained QPS / tokens-per-second to validate batching efficiency.
- Confirm SLA for the hold: are you asking for a no-cost 72-hour soft-hold then conversion to a paid standby, or do you require a reserved/committed block for the full four weeks?

I'll kick off an internal availability check with Infra & Fleet (CC'ing Marcus & Aditya). Once they confirm, I'll send a provisional hold notice that expires 2029-10-28 as requested.

Quick note on terms: our standard provisional hold is a 10% capacity buffer for up to two weeks at no charge while procurement moves; for holds longer than two weeks we typically require a nominal standby fee (credited if the PO converts within the window). If you need an exception, we can escalate.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference runtime
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Oct 2029 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: AEQ standby sizing & hold request — please validate availability

Team — quick internal coordination. External asked for provisional hold: 18 A100-80GB equiv for 4 weeks starting ~2029-11-04. They want the hold to stand until 2029-10-28 while procurement wraps.

Key constraints / asks:
- Target p99 latency <700ms. Workload is 70B quantized (4-bit) — advise whether we should recommend 70B -> 70B-8bit or 40B fallback variant for cost/availability.
- They listed concurrency ~35 sessions with ~900 tokens each. Please run a quick capacity sketch (nodes, expected throughput, prewarm time) and flag any conflicts with committed Dedicated pools.
- If we can spare the 18-GPU-equivalent, I'd like a recommended conservative allocation (include a 15% buffer) and an estimate of runbook steps to convert standby -> committed.

Marcus: can you confirm inventory in us-west for the requested window and whether we can map this to a mix of 8x and 4x nodes?
Aditya: cost/quantization advise — if we recommend fallback to a 40B quantized variant, what unit token delta / quality risk should we expect?

I'll hold on the provisional hold note until I get your replies (aiming to send to external by EOD tomorrow).

Thanks — Hannah
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Oct 2029 11:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: AEQ standby sizing & hold request — please validate availability

Hannah — quick availability snapshot for us-west (preliminary):

Inventory window (2029-11-04 -> 2029-12-02)
- Free equivalent capacity today: ~26 A100-80GB equivalents across pooled nodes. However, 8 of those are already earmarked for Dedicated commitments the week of Nov 11-18 (committed by another customer).
- That leaves a practical pool of ~18 equiv, but we should not fully exhaust fleet. Recommended conservative allocation: 15 equiv for AEQ with a 15% buffer = 17 equiv reserved.

Node mapping proposal:
- Preferred: 4 x 4-node 80GB hosts (4 GPUs/host) = 16 GPUs; plus 1 spare GPU for buffer (total 17).
- Prewarm time: ~90 minutes to load model weights and KV caches at scale for 70B 4-bit. Recommend we schedule prewarm in a rolling manner to avoid cold-start spikes.

Fallbacks & mitigation:
- If inventory tightens, we can offer a 40B-4bit fallback variant mapped to the same pool with a smaller per-GPU memory footprint; expect ~10-15% increased throughput but a small quality regression on some instruction-following prompts.
- If AEQ requires strict p99 <700ms, we should limit concurrency via session throttles and increase batching RPS target.

Next steps: I can place a provisional hold for 17-equiv (label: AEQ-standby-A) that expires 2029-10-28. If procurement signs before that, we convert to a Reserved allocation and update routing/pinning.

Marcus
Senior Capacity Planner | Redwood Inference
